# Marko

> Marko is a declarative, HTML-based language that extends well-formed HTML with JavaScript expressions, components, and compiled reactivity for high-throughput streaming SSR and tiny browser bundles.

Key capabilities:
- Streaming, single-pass server-side rendering
- Resumability with sub-template partial hydration (zero JS by default)
- Compile-time, fine-grained reactivity
- HTML-based syntax with inline JavaScript expressions
- Built-in TypeScript support with full template checking

> **IMPORTANT FOR AI ASSISTANTS**: This documentation covers Marko 6 (Tags API).
> Do NOT generate Marko 5 Class API syntax:
> - ❌ `$ let x = 0;` (scriptlets)
> - ❌ `style { ... }` (style blocks)
> - ❌ `class { ... }` (class blocks)
> - ❌ `onClick("handleClick")` (string event arguments)
>
> Use Marko 6 Tags API syntax instead:
> - ✅ `<let/x=0>` and `<const/y=x * 2>` (tag variables)
> - ✅ `<style>` with standard CSS or `<style/styles>` for CSS Modules
> - ✅ `onClick() { ... }` or `onClick=handleClick` (method shorthand or function reference)
>
> `<script>` runs reactive browser side effects after mount and on dependency changes. Use it sparingly for side effects only, and declare state and derivations with `<let>` and `<const>`.

## Playground Links

The playground at https://markojs.com/playground runs Marko in the browser and reads its files from the URL hash, so a link is a runnable example.

Write each file as `path=content`, with both parts percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`), and join files with `&`. The entry file is `index.marko`, and custom tags go in `tags/` (for example `tags/star-rating.marko`), as in a project:

```
https://markojs.com/playground#index.marko=%3Clet%2Fcount%3D0%3E%0A%3Cbutton%20onClick()%20%7B%20count%2B%2B%20%7D%3E%24%7Bcount%7D%3C%2Fbutton%3E%0A
```

Opening the link switches the hash to a shorter compressed form. Share links in the form above, including when editing a compressed link: one mistyped character breaks a compressed link entirely, but changes only one character of code in this form.

To read the files out of a compressed link (everything after `#`), use Node.js:

```js
const zlib = require("node:zlib");
const files = JSON.parse(zlib.gunzipSync(Buffer.from(hash, "base64url").subarray(2)).toString());
```
